name: tariff-tune
prompt:
`large_total(2)` sums station 2's billed amounts that are strictly above `cutoff`. Find the LARGEST whole-number `cutoff` for which `large_total(2)` is still at least 20000. The answer is somewhere between 0 and 1200.

You cannot work this out by reading the code, because the readings are generated rather than written down. You have to probe for it: a binary search is the sensible way.

HOW TO SEARCH. Always change the value of the EXISTING `cutoff` binding with `update_definition`. Never add a second `cutoff`, and do not introduce any new bindings; the search is only over that one number.

After each change, find out what the program actually came to before choosing your next guess -- either by inspecting it with your tools, or by ending your turn, in which case you will be told the value and can carry on from there. Changing the number several times in a row without looking at any of the results tells you nothing.

When you are confident you have the exact answer, say DONE.
expectation:
Built to separate a2 from aPL, which no other task in this set does.

The search itself is the same shape as tune-threshold, but the program is organised differently: the expensive per-station work (`from_station` then `map`) is reached through a CALL to `billed_amounts` inside `large_total`'s body, rather than sitting in a top-level let. That matters because aPL's cache admits only expressions evaluated at the empty callstack (Calculus.callstack_depth_limit is 0 for aPL, 4 for a2), so under aPL nothing inside a function call is ever cached and the aggregation is redone on every guess. a2 keys entries by (callstack, id) and re-uses it.

On a synthetic trace of six cutoff changes over this program the gap was large: a0 568ms, aPL 218ms (0.384), a2 15ms (0.027) -- a2 roughly 14x faster than aPL. The pre-existing hand-written bench/traces/callstack.json shows the same effect more starkly still (aPL 0.914, a2 0.395), because there even the base data sits under a call.

This is also the honest qualifier on yesterday's five tasks: they all put the expensive work in top-level bindings, which is precisely the case aPL already handles, so a2 looked unremarkable. Which calculus wins depends on how the program under test is organised, not only on what the edit does.

NOTE: `goal` is an oracle the agent never sees. Expected answer is cutoff 434, at which large_total(2) is 20699.
